# Phase Two — Gevurah Critique: Twenty-Two Corrections

The Awtsmoos gives measure to abundance so the vessel does not break,
Awtsmoos.com must turn a million bright ideas into changes users safely take.
The first brainstorm sought every horizon; this pass removes the tempting excess,
So SEO becomes truthful architecture and UX becomes clarity rather than dress.

## Twenty-two improvements to the first plan

1. Do not create a second SEO framework. Extend the production-wired `PublicHtmlSeo` pipeline already serving exact generated metadata.
2. Do not hand-edit 100+ HTML entries. Improve shared server transforms and generated truth sources so coverage scales with the catalog.
3. Preserve the repo's deliberate generated-RDFa contract; do not replace it with JSON-LD merely for fashion.
4. Detect authored JSON-LD, microdata, and RDFa before adding generated primary structured data so authored truth remains sovereign.
5. Keep generated schema factual: no fabricated ratings, prices, dates, authors, images, or freshness.
6. Strengthen the schema graph with a typed WebSite relationship rather than only a bare `isPartOf` URL.
7. Add hierarchy only where it is certain. Apps and Games have stable parent hubs; arbitrary path-segment breadcrumbs could invent meaning.
8. Avoid forced global headers. Full-screen apps and games have specialist layouts that a generic header could damage.
9. Improve missing keyboard escape routes instead: conditional skip-to-main enhancement is nearly invisible visually and high-value ergonomically.
10. Preserve every authored skip link. Generated accessibility must fill gaps, never replace page-specific wording or targets.
11. Add missing viewport metadata centrally for complete HTML documents; mobile usability should not depend on each legacy page remembering it.
12. Never assume a language globally. Translation routes and mixed-language Torah content make a forced `lang=en` unsafe.
13. Keep universal CSS low-specificity and semantic. Do not repaint classed specialist components.
14. Add global focus visibility carefully so classed custom controls remain operable even when their local CSS forgot keyboard states.
15. Add high-contrast/forced-color fallbacks rather than increasing decoration or visual noise.
16. Preserve the modular CSS source tree. Production `compact=true` already folds imports into one dependency-aware response, so source modularity does not imply a request waterfall.
17. Do not rewrite the actively modified home, Apps, or Games HTML unless a verified central mechanism cannot solve the issue.
18. Keep unknown HTML pass-through semantics in the SEO transformer; private/internal pages must not accidentally become indexable because they are reachable.
19. Add tests only after implementation, matching the repository's code-first contract.
20. Verify both raw transformed HTML and browser behavior; hydration success alone cannot prove crawlable head/body semantics.
21. Re-run generated metadata/sitemap coverage after code changes even if no generator source changes, because central semantics can expose assumptions the existing audit missed.
22. Measure touched-file size before finalizing; any file that crosses the project's modularity ceiling must split instead of compressing comments or functions.

## Architecture after critique

Keep the existing production graph and add three narrow layers:

- SEO evidence layer: robust authored-structured-data recognition plus a richer truthful site graph.
- HTML essentials layer: viewport and conditional skip navigation for every complete non-raw document.
- Universal usability layer: one small low-specificity accessibility stylesheet imported by the existing compact universal bundle.

No page-by-page rewrite is justified at this stage.

## NEXT_ACTION

Map exact affected modules, inspect existing document-transform helpers/tests, and produce a second file-level plan before the third critique.
